content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The overall structure is sound and idiomatic: `AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate` mirrors its sibling `AssignOwnerBulkSignupWarning`/`AssignOwnerNamesakeCount` functions (single `service(@Val Owner, OwnerRepository)`, mutate in place, `findAll().stream()`), it's slotted into the pipeline at the right spot (after `BuildOwner`, before `SaveOwner`), the Javadoc explains the ordering rationale, and the model/schema (all four dialects)/OpenAPI are all updated consistently. Good, additive work overall. Two duplication nits worth fixing:

1. **`AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate.java:50-52` — the private `equals(String, String)` helper reimplements `java.util.Objects.equals`.** The body `a == null ? b == null : a.equals(b)` is exactly `Objects.equals(a, b)`. Drop the helper and call `java.util.Objects.equals(...)` directly — it's the idiomatic, zero-cost choice and removes a method a maintainer has to read to confirm it does nothing surprising.

2. **`AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate.java:46-48` — the null-safe `equalsIgnoreCase` helper is now a verbatim copy of the one in `AssignOwnerNamesakeCount.java:24-26`.** The same null-safe case-insensitive comparison now lives in two owner functions. Since this codebase already extracts small shared concerns into helper types (`IdentityKey`, `HouseholdKey`, `CustomerCode`, `TelephoneNormalizer`, `EmailNormalizer`), lifting this into a shared utility (or reusing one) and having both classes call it would be the natural fit and stops the pattern from being copy-pasted a third time.

Neither affects where the logic lives — the function itself is in the right unit; these are just local de-duplication cleanups.
